name: El Ceibillo
summary: Licensed for a 25 MW first-phase flash plant between Volcán de Agua and Pacaya, structurally controlled by faulting related to the Mixco Fault within the Guatemala City graben. 22 wells drilled to date; up to 274°C measured at depth. Conceptual model places a shallow 200–400m-deep, ~200°C target above a deeper resource that still needs drilling below 1200m to test its permeability.
detail: Quaternary-Tertiary volcanics sit on a Cretaceous granitic basement, with heatflow tied to Holocene volcanism and upflow channelled along structures related to the Mixco Fault. The Bouguer gravity survey below defines two cross-section lines through the field — A-A′, running SE from the EC-4/EC-3/EC-5 cluster through EC-1 to the B-series wells, and B-B′, cutting the opposite way across EC-8 through to TG-9 — built from a two-tier conceptual model: a shallow reservoir in fractured rhyolite, volcanic breccia, andesite and granite beneath a clay cap, with 230°C measured directly at 1170m depth and a deeper, down-dip fracture target projected between 600–900m that still needs drilling to confirm.
